elements.element: Vendor must defend covered claims.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly agrees to “defend” against the claims described in subsection (c).

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify against covered claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly agrees to “indemnify and hold harmless” and covers resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Customer must be an indemnified party.
elements.evidence: The Company is expressly protected.

elements.element: Customer’s affiliates must be indemnified parties.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly protects the Company’s affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor’s defense and indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The opening language expressly applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Covered IP claims must include allegations that Vendor’s services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause covers the Site and materials, software, or technology provided by HDI, but it does not expressly cover all services, such as hosting or other service activities.

elements.element: Covered IP claims must include allegations that Vendor’s deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The Site and materials, software, and technology provided by HDI are covered for alleged infringement or misappropriation of any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c)(ii) expressly covers “HDI’s breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c)(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Content or customer or user data caused by HDI.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c)(iv) expressly covers HDI’s gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c)(iv) expressly covers HDI’s willful misconduct; the spelling difference is immaterial.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No claim-notice procedure is included.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defense and settlement of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: The clause does not allocate control of defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation or procedure is included.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must not extend beyond claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered language imposes no indemnification obligation on the Company, so there is no broader Customer indemnity in this clause.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer for covered IP claims.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly indemnifies the Company for the IP claims described in subsection (c)(i).

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) expressly applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must cover allegations that Vendor’s services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause identifies the Site and HDI-provided materials, software, or technology but does not expressly cover all Vendor services.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must cover allegations that Vendor’s deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The Site and HDI-provided materials, software, and technology are covered for alleged infringement or misappropriation.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion for modifications made by the Company or another party.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: There is no combination exclusion.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Customer-provided specifications or instructions.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion for compliance with Company specifications or instructions.

elements.element: For infringing services or deliverables, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to procure the right for Customer to continue using them.
elements.evidence: No procurement-of-rights remedy is included.

elements.element: For infringing services or deliverables, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to modify them so they become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy is included.

elements.element: For infringing services or deliverables, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to replace them with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy is included.

elements.element: For infringing services or deliverables, Vendor must provide a refund remedy if the other infringement remedies are unavailable or impracticable.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy is included.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no liability cap or cross-reference imposing a three-times-annual-fees super-cap. Although uncapped liability is more favorable to the Company, the specified fallback cap is not operative.

result.reason: The redline is focused and preserves the existing Globix provision while adding a coherent Vendor indemnity. It covers most preferred substantive triggers, but it omits the required notice, defense-control, and cooperation procedures and does not expressly cover all Vendor services. It also fails the fallback because the usual IP exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The margin comment does not cure these operative omissions.
